706483.t: Verbal abstract from ἰδεῖν (ĭdeîn, aor. of ὁράω (horắō)), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *weyd- (“to see”). Closely related to εἶδος (eîdos).

706493.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *hwédios, from Proto-Indo-European *swéd-yo-s, from *swé (“self”). Equivalent to ἕ (hé) + -ιος (-ĭos).

706424.t: Uncertain, but frequently compared to ἰαίνω (iaínō, “to warm”), with both often derived from Proto-Indo-European *h₁eysh₂- (“to strengthen, propel”).

706458.t: From ἰατρός (īātrós, “physician”), from ἰάομαι (iáomai, “I cure, treat”).

706497.t: From ἰδοῦ (ĭdoû), aorist middle imperative second singular form of ὁράω (horáō, “to see, to find out, to make sure”).

706451.t: A loanword of unclear source, but possibly Egyptian in origin. Compare Biblical Hebrew יָשְׁפֵה (yāšəfēh, “jasper”), Amarna Akkadian 𒉌𒌓𒅀𒀸𒁍 (/⁠yašpû⁠/, “name of a stone”) (whence Classical Syriac ܝܫܦܐ (jaʃpɑ(ʔ), “jasper”)).

706479.t: A hypostasis *ἐν-γνύ-α (*en-gnú-a, “place in the knee”). The stem ἰγνύς (ignús) was formed after ἰξύς (ixús, “waist, loins”) and ὀσφῦς (osphûs, “hips or loins”).

706457.t: From ἰατρεύω (īātreúō, “to treat medically, to cure”) + -εῖον (-eîon).

706494.t: From ἴδιος (ĭ́dĭos, “one’s own; peculiar”) + -της (-tēs, abstract noun suffix).
